newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end firmer, off early lows.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end firmer, off early lows.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended higher on Thursday, recovering from midday lows as the yen's fall late in the day fuelled active buying ahead of the close, traders said.
Prices ranged from flat to 290 yen per tonne firmer. The most-active contract, benchmark March, was up 200 yen at 16,520 yen. Daily volume was estimated at 82,265 lots.
The market opened firmer, following moderate gains in the Chicago overnight market. Prices fell at midday and then recovered, but traders said that the Chicago market remains fundamentally bearish.
The May corn futures contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system was quoted at $2.82-3/4 per bushel at 0824 GMT, compared with $2.83-1/2 on Wednesday.
The March soybean contract on the overnight trading system was quoted at $7.72 per bushel, against $7.71 on Wednesday.
